instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: The lexicon entries bear the grouping out: the codes with the largest counts are the verbs of thinking and supposing (G1380 to think, G3543 to think, G3633 and G5282 to suppose, G5274 to take up, suppose) and the verb to say, whose Qal sense in the lexicon includes saying in one's heart and so thinking (H0559, the largest code with 40 occurrences), with H2803J (think, imagine), H1819 (to imagine, think), H2803I (to plan, devise), H5452 (to think, intend) and H6245B (to think). H0194 'perhaps, suppose' gives the case put forward. Codes that link the group to its usage: H0559 for the thought quoted to oneself and G1380 and G3543 for the supposition acted on. The group definition is a supposition or estimate held. Codes in these units that do not carry the meaning themselves, because the unit aligns a neighbouring word into it, are the connectives and function words (G1161, G2532, H3588A, H0834A, H0413, H0853, H1931, H2009, H1961); the lexicon gives them their own senses (then, and, for, which, to, the object marker, he, behold, to be), and stage 1 read them in their verses.

Desire words stand with the group in 1Sa 18:25, 1Ch 28:9 and Jam 4:5: 'desires' 12 words before in 1Sa 18:25, 'willing' 9 before in 1Ch 28:9, 'yearns' 5 after in Jam 4:5. The surface 'will' of 2Sa 14:17 (4 after) and 2Ki 7:12 (13 before) is the particle and verb of the quoted speech, not a desire.

Heart or mind stands with the group in all ten verses. It is within three words of the member in Deu 15:9 and 2Sa 13:33 (1), Isa 10:7 (2), Eze 20:32 and Rom 1:21 (3); at 4 in 1Ch 28:9 (hearts), Mat 9:4 and 1Ti 6:5; at 6 in Eze 11:5; and at 10 in Jam 1:26 and 1Ch 28:9 (heart). The verses name the heart or mind as the place of the thought.

Intending stands with the group in 1Ch 28:9, Psa 64:5, Isa 10:7, Joh 11:13, Act 27:13 and Jam 4:5. The partner words are of the same kind as the member in 1Ch 28:9 (plan, 1 before), Psa 64:5 (purpose, 4 before) and Isa 10:7 (intend, 4 before); in Joh 11:13 'meant' is 2 after and is what Jesus meant, which they supposed otherwise; in Act 27:13 and Jam 4:5 'purpose' is 2 and 1 after.

Knowing stands with the group in thirteen verses. In 1Cor 8:2 (knows 1 after, know 5 after) and Ecc 9:10 (knowledge 1 after) knowledge is beside the member; in Mat 9:4 and Eze 11:5 what is known is another's thought (Jesus knowing their thoughts, the Lord knowing what comes into the mind); in 1Sa 20:3 the knowing (6 before, 3 after) is the father's knowledge of David's favour and Jonathan's not knowing; elsewhere it is 3 to 15 words away (Exo 2:14, Rut 4:4, 2Ki 7:12, 1Ch 28:9, Act 12:9, Rom 1:21, Rom 14:14, 2Cor 10:5).

Searching and finding stand with the group in ten verses. In Gen 18:28 and Gen 18:30 'find' is the condition of each supposed number (positions not stored); in Mat 18:12 (17 after), Luk 2:44 (9 after) and Joh 20:15 the search follows or acts on the supposition; in Joh 5:39 the search of the Scriptures is 4 words before the supposition; in 1Ch 28:9 the Lord searches hearts (6 before) and 'seek' is 2 after.

Doing and serving stand with the group in twelve verses. 'Do' is the partner in nine: Gen 18:29 and 18:30 (positions not stored), Num 33:56 (1 after), Luk 12:17 (4 after), Rom 2:3 (7 after), Eze 18:14 (11 after), 1Cor 7:36 (10 after), Ecc 9:10 (5 before) and Eph 3:20 (8 before); in Num 33:56 and Luk 12:17 the doing is what is purposed or asked within 4 words of the thought. 'Serve' is the partner in 1Ch 28:9 (12 before), Joh 16:2 (service, 2 after, which the killer supposes he offers) and Phili 2:25 (minister, 16 after).

Wisdom and understanding stand with the group in eight verses. The partner is within two words in Pro 14:15 (prudent, 1 before), Psa 73:16 (understand, 1 after), Ecc 9:10 (wisdom, 2 after) and 1Cor 3:18 (wise, 2 after); in 1Cor 3:18 the person thinks that he is wise, so wisdom is what is thought of oneself. In 1Ch 28:9 (3 before), 2Sa 14:17 (12 after), Rom 2:3 (11 after) and 1Cor 7:40 (7 before) the partner is farther off.

Qualifiers stand with the supposing group in 58 verses with negators (79 stored pairs) and in many more with adjectives and adverbs. The negator reaches the member itself, forbidding, denying or withholding the supposition, in Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34 and Joh 5:45 (do not think, 1 word before), Act 17:29, Jam 1:7, 2Cor 11:16, 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33, Rom 12:3 (not to think too highly of oneself), Isa 10:7 and Lam 1:9. In Jos 22:28, 1Sa 20:26, 2Sa 5:6, Neh 6:9, Mat 26:53, Joh 11:56, Act 13:25, Luk 12:17 and Jon 1:6 the negator is inside the supposed or quoted content and reaches another word of it. In Mat 6:7, 1Cor 14:20, Act 12:9, Phili 1:17, Rom 1:21, 1Cor 8:2, Jam 1:26, Eze 20:32 and Act 2:15 it stands in the same sentence and reaches another verb (heap up, be children, know, sincerely, honor, know, bridle, happen, drunk); adjacency is not scope. Of the adjectives and adverbs, the ones that qualify the supposing itself are 'again' (Gen 18:32), 'now' (2Ch 13:8), 'so' (Isa 10:7, Eze 11:5), 'all along' (2Cor 12:19) and 'otherwise' (Phili 3:15); most of the rest, such as wise, unclean, religious, incredible and necessary, qualify the state of affairs that is supposed.

Entities are named in 89 of the 155 verses of the supposing group, 62 different ones in 187 stored pairs (118 human, 69 divine). The divine are God (31), the Lord (21), Jesus (8), Christ (5), the Most High and the possessive forms. The human are mostly the figures of the narratives who think or suppose: David (19), Saul (8), Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Hanun, Hezekiah, Naaman, Esther, Mordecai, Judas and many others, with man, men and brothers. This group names far more persons than any other group of thought (the next largest has 25 different entities); the other groups name God, the Lord and Jesus, and a few persons each.

The direction of the supposing changes across the verses. In most the supposer is a named person who holds a view about another person or a state of affairs: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Saul, David, Naaman and Hezekiah hold a quoted thought, with the human entity before the member in 72 of 118 human pairs. In Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42 and Luk 10:36 the direction is reversed: Jesus asks the hearer what he thinks. Toward God it runs in Psa 50:21 (you thought I was like yourself), Act 17:29 and Jon 1:6 (perhaps the god will give a thought to us), and from the Lord to the people in Eze 11:5.

Knowing and the supposition meet in thirteen verses with different ties. In 1Cor 8:2 (1 to 8 words after) and Ecc 9:10 (1 after) knowledge is what the person thinks he has or what is absent; in Mat 9:4 and Eze 11:5 the thinking is known by another; elsewhere the knowing is 3 to 15 words away in separate clauses (Exo 2:14, Rut 4:4, 2Ki 7:12, 1Ch 28:9, Act 12:9, Rom 1:21, Rom 14:14, 2Cor 10:5).

Searching and finding stand with the supposition in ten verses. In Gen 18:28 and 18:30 'find' is the condition of each supposed number; in Joh 20:15 the seeking is 1 word before the supposition; in Joh 5:39 the search of the Scriptures is 4 words before; in Mat 18:12 (17 after), Luk 2:44 (9 after), 2Sa 10:3 and 1Ch 19:3 the search is in a later clause; in 1Ch 28:9 the Lord searches hearts 6 words before.

Doing and serving stand with the supposition in twelve verses. 'Do' is the partner in nine verses (ten words, two of them in Num 33:56): Num 33:56 (1 after, 3 before), Luk 12:17 (4 after), Gen 18:29 and 18:30 (6 and 9 after), Rom 2:3, 1Cor 7:36, Eze 18:14, Ecc 9:10, Eph 3:20; 'serve' is 12 words before in 1Ch 28:9, 'service' is 2 words after in Joh 16:2 and 'minister' 16 after in Phili 2:25. In Num 33:56 and Luk 12:17 the doing is what is purposed or asked within four words of the thought.

Wisdom and understanding stand with the supposition in eight verses. The partner is within two words in Pro 14:15 (prudent, 1 before), Psa 73:16 (understand, 1 after), Ecc 9:10 (wisdom, 2 after) and 1Cor 3:18 (wise, 2 after), where the person thinks that he is wise; in 1Ch 28:9 (3 before), 2Sa 14:17 (12 after), Rom 2:3 (11 after) and 1Cor 7:40 (7 before) the partner is farther off.
